deaths.description: Motor-vehicle crash deaths 2017-2023 (sum of FARS FATALS, county of crash)

population.description: 2020 Census resident population (exposure; person-years = 7 x population)

personYears.description: Population at risk, person-years over the 7 years

fatalCrashes.description: Number of fatal crashes in the 7 years

ruralDeaths.description: Deaths in crashes coded rural (FARS RUR_URB=1)

rawRate.description: Raw annual deaths per 100,000 residents (unsmoothed: unstable where population is small)

properties.alignedTo: us-counties (same row order, sorted by FIPS)
properties.event: Motor-vehicle traffic crash deaths (FARS), county where the crash occurred
properties.usage: Empirical Bayes: counts = deaths, population at risk = personYears (or population). Rate = deaths / personYears.
properties.why: CDC WONDER cannot be fetched programmatically and CDC county overdose data suppress counts of 1-9; FARS has exact unsuppressed counts for every county.
caveats: Counts are deaths by county of crash, not residence; population is 2020 Census residents, so tourist/transit counties are inflated.
Connecticut crashes are assigned to the 9 planning regions by crash latitude/longitude (raw 5m boundaries); Alaska/Hawaii excluded.
Crashes with a county code that does not match a us-counties FIPS are dropped.
properties.sources: NHTSA FARS 2017-2023 final annual files (static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS), public domain; population: US Census 2020 via USDA ERS
storyNotes: 275,368 deaths in 7 years; national raw rate 11.9 per 100k per year.

Small counties (<5,000 residents, n=307): raw rates range 7-174 per 100k (5th-95th pct) vs 5-21 for counties over 100,000 (n=599); the spread is mostly sampling noise, ideal for empirical Bayes shrinkage.
Highest raw rates (mostly tiny counties, unreliable): Loving, TX 6027; Kenedy, TX 612; Esmeralda, NV 510; Glasscock, TX 346; Mineral, CO 314.
Highest raw rates among counties over 100,000 residents: Robeson, NC 48.3; Navajo, AZ 40.3; Coconino, AZ 34.3; Ector, TX 29.9.
8 counties had zero deaths in 7 years (rate exactly 0, a classic EB artefact); 355 had fewer than 10.
